title: The Design of Poison and Mirage
notes: Detective-cast (Hattori Heiji, Kazuha, Conan, Ran, Kogoro, and recurring police officer Takagi) omitted by convention. Case spans episodes 652-655; only subs_resolved/0652.txt and subs_resolved/0655.txt are available locally (653 and 654 are missing), so the middle of the investigation is not directly attested -- this file is built only from what 652 and 655 state or recap, nothing invented to fill the gap. Known specific gap: the exact mechanism by which Serika concealed the original bloody dying-message tiles at the Karuizawa villa (a tile-swap like the Osaka decoy, or something else) is never spelled out on-screen in the surviving episodes, only that she 'hid the evidence' -- clue o1/edges around it are marked accordingly. The old lower-fidelity case file (cases/ep652-655_the_design_of_poison_and_mirage.json) correctly names Satake Yoshimi as the poisoner of both Ikuro and Serika, but it omits the actual engine of her motive: the transcript reveals that Ikuro Wakamatsu himself stabbed his father Kohei to death at the Karuizawa villa a month before episode 652, and that Serika (Kohei's wife) covered it up by hiding the bloody dying-message evidence -- neither fact appears in the old file, which treats Kohei's death only as an inert unsolved backstory event with no named killer. Satake is revealed to be Kohei's secret biological daughter from his first marriage, avenging both her father's murder and its cover-up. No event nodes: every action is a direct typed edge between the people/locations/objects involved. case_type: murder (triple).

clues.desc: Fujinami switched the plastic bottle to his off hand for a plain reason (checking his watch); Satake never once used her left hand at all, and her bronze watch -- clean before -- now shows fresh shine where cyanide from the dictionary reacted with the metal in wash water.

The vanished dying message read only 'S' before Kohei's hand blocked the rest; Shiina, Sumio (Fujinami), Satake, Serika and Sakurako (Yonehara) all have an 'S' initial, so the letter alone accuses everyone and no one.
